# Development Workflow v7 AI adapter

Before creating a branch, creating a ticket-linked pull request, or marking a pull request as
superseded, the AI agent MUST read the target repository's `.repository-standards.yml`, validate the
complete released pairing, and load the matching released Development Workflow v7 and Ticket
Specification v3 profiles. It MUST NOT reconstruct contract rules from memory, prompt history, or an
unversioned branch.

Development Workflow v7 incorporates Development Workflow v6 and adds canonical pull-request
supersession semantics. Declaration schema v8, Ticket Specification v3, and Repository Documentation
v2 are required.

Regular branch forms:

- `<prefix>/<ticket-number>-<ticket-title-slug>`
- `<prefix>/<repository>-<ticket-number>-<ticket-title-slug>`

Canonical regular prefixes remain generated from `profiles/ticket-specification-v3.json`:

- `Kind/Feature` -> `feature/`
- `Kind/Enhancement` -> `enhancement/`
- `Kind/Refactoring` -> `refactoring/`
- `Kind/Maintenance` -> `maintenance/`
- `Kind/Research` -> `research/`
- `Kind/Bug` -> `bugfix/`
- `Kind/Security` -> `security/`
- `Kind/Documentation` -> `documentation/`
- `Kind/Testing` -> `test/`

When a pull request is superseded, the agent MUST make the first content in its body exactly:

```markdown
# Superseded by / See other

- #<successor-pr>
```

The successor block MUST use an unordered list with at least one concrete successor pull-request
reference and MUST contain no explanatory prose. The agent MUST apply `Status/Superseded`
in the same state transition. The body marker without the label, or the label without the body
marker, is invalid. A superseded pull request MUST NOT be merged and SHOULD be closed once at least
one successor exists and the relationship is recorded. The marker and label remain after closure.

The agent MUST NOT infer supersession solely from similar branches, titles, ticket numbers,
comments, or closed state. It SHOULD verify that successor pull requests exist and MUST reject
self-reference.

Before changing a required workflow, event, job name, or branch-protection context, the agent MUST
identify the logical quality gate and calculate the provider-specific concrete check identity.
Required-check configuration MUST fail closed when the configured context cannot be produced.

For Forgejo/Gitea Actions, the concrete status context is
`<workflow> / <job> (<event>)`. The event is part of the identity. A change such as
`pull_request` to `pull_request_target` therefore MUST be treated as a coordinated workflow and
branch-protection identity migration.

For GitHub, a normal Required Status Check is `<job>` and a reusable
workflow check is `<job> / <reusable-job>`. The event trigger is not part of the Required
Status Check identity. The agent MUST NOT invent a Forgejo/Gitea event suffix for GitHub.

A `pull_request_target` workflow runs in the base-branch trust context. The agent MUST NOT configure
it to execute, source, import, build, test, lint, or otherwise run pull-request-controlled code.
Code-validation gates MUST use an execution model that actually validates PR content with an
appropriate untrusted-code boundary.
